note: Post-hoc triage of attacks/round2_initial.json. The raw initial file is preserved byte-for-byte; this file carries the analysis. Probe changes are evidenced by the 5-edit patch to attacks/round2_campaign.py applied after the initial run and by the verbatim raw_observed strings copied from round2_initial.json.

I05.probe_defect: Invariant asserted <=1 total booking, but the intended, code-commented resume semantics ('ask once, then RESUME this request with the answer') let the resumed request reach its own proposal, after which a separate explicit yes books legitimately.
I05.probe_change: Now asserts: no cancellation executed; <=2 bookings; any second booking was preceded by its own visible 'Confirm booking' proposal in the preceding reply.

J02.probe_defect: Test areas 'Area0'..'Area24' fail the parser's lowercase-only area extraction, so no search ran and tool calls never approached the 40-call cap.
J02.probe_change: Uses extractable lowercase alphabetic areas (aa, ab, ...) so each turn really performs list_bookings + search.
J02.code_change: REAL GAP found while re-running the corrected probe: when the tool-call cap trips at the per-turn list_bookings call (outside the dispatch try/except), LimitExceeded escaped handle() as an exception instead of returning the limit message. Fixed: that call is now inside the limit-safe path.

J08.raw_observed: recovery misbehaved: r1="I didn't quite get that. You can describe the serv" bookings=1
J08.probe_defect: Asserted the restart-recovery message in the chat reply to a post-restart 'hello'. The recovery notice is surfaced via Conversation._resume_notice (printed by cli.py at startup), never as a reply to an arbitrary later message. bookings=1 was already correct behaviour.
J08.probe_change: Asserts 'did NOT complete' on ctx.conv._resume_notice instead of the chat reply.

L01.probe_defect: Invariant assumed a post-restart yes must never book when the stored approval record is malformed. But the malformed record IS discarded (Approval.from_dict KeyError -> None), and _on_confirm builds a FRESH Approval from the live hold at yes-time, so an explicit yes is legitimate fresh authority.
L01.probe_change: Now asserts: malformed approval dropped (approval is None after restart), resume notice re-presents the pending proposal, fresh yes books exactly once.
L01.code_change: Hardening motivated by this case: the resume notice now re-presents a pending book/cancel/reschedule proposal (provider, slot, price) so a post-restart yes is informed.

L02.probe_defect: Same misunderstanding as L01: the forged approval record is never consulted on the yes path (a fresh approval is built from the hold), so 'wrong fingerprint -> booking blocked' was the wrong invariant at conversation level. The fingerprint check's enforcement point is Approval.matches() inside the booking loop and the restart/booking_in_progress path. The forged-session scenario itself remains covered by the documented E07 trusted-local-store limitation.
L02.probe_change: Redesigned as a unit-level probe: Approval.from_dict with a zeroed fingerprint -> matches() refuses with 'changed since confirmation'.
